# Copilot Instructions

These instructions are generated from the project's CLAUDE.md and available skills
so that GitHub Copilot CLI follows the same conventions as other agents.

Paths shown as `$CODING_REPO` refer to the root of this repository.
Paths shown as `~` refer to the user's home directory.

## Project Guidelines


## Mandatory Rules

- **PlantUML**: Use `plantuml` CLI command. NEVER `java -jar plantuml.jar`
- **TypeScript**: Mandatory with strict type checking
- **API design**: Never modify working APIs for TypeScript compliance; fix types instead
- **Visual UI verification — use `gsd-browser`**: For visual smoke/screenshot/click-through against `localhost:3002`/`3032`/`8080` or any local web UI, use the `gsd-browser` CLI (`navigate`, `screenshot`, `click`, `eval`, `select-frame`, `snapshot`) — wraps Playwright with the correct chromium resolution, avoids `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` from inline `chromium.launch()` scripts. `/playwright-cli` is an allowed entry point but a hand-rolled `node /tmp/foo.mjs` Playwright script still violates `prefer-gsd-browser`. Structured E2E tests go under `tests/e2e/<area>/<spec>.spec.ts`, run via `npx playwright test`.
- **gsd-browser MUST NOT drive the user's own Chrome bundle** — `~/.gsd-browser/config.toml` pins `[browser] path` to Playwright's "Google Chrome for Testing" (bundle id `com.google.chrome.for.testing`) via the `~/.gsd-browser/chromium.app` symlink. Apple Events are addressed by BUNDLE ID, so two live instances of `com.google.Chrome` are indistinguishable to AppleScript and the automation one answers FIRST: every `tell application "Google Chrome"` on the machine silently retargets into the headless profile. That is what broke the status-line click handler — it found a dashboard tab, navigated it and reported `reused idx=9 active=9` against a browser nobody could see, for hours, with no error anywhere. It also defeats its own verification, since asking AppleScript what happened asks the wrong browser too; only a screenshot from the user caught it. The daemon leaks (`daemon stop` reports success and stops nothing), so one screenshot run shadows every AppleScript on the machine until the next reboot. Config keys follow the env names (`GSD_BROWSER_BROWSER_PATH` → `[browser] path`); `browser_path` is silently IGNORED. The symlink must point at the `.app`, never the binary inside it — Chrome resolves `../Frameworks` from argv[0]'s directory and dies with a dlopen error otherwise. Playwright deletes old revisions on upgrade, so re-point it if gsd-browser stops launching: `ln -sfn ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium-*/chrome-mac-arm64/"Google Chrome for Testing.app" ~/.gsd-browser/chromium.app`. `install.sh` applies this pin on macOS only — Linux and Windows have no Apple Event routing, so two Chrome instances there cannot intercept one another and reusing a system Chrome is correct. **`bin/statusline-click` is likewise per-platform**: macOS gets AppleScript tab reuse, Linux `xdg-open`/`gio open`, WSL `wslview`/`cmd.exe start`, Windows `start`. Reuse is macOS-only (no scripting bridge elsewhere) — a new tab is the honest ceiling. Every branch ends in a launched browser or a message in the pane, and the handler ALWAYS exits 0, because tmux renders a failing `run-shell` as a view the user must dismiss.
- **gsd-browser has TWO failure modes and they look nothing alike.** (a) *Daemon won't start / `receiver is gone`* — stale runner lock: `pkill -9 -f "chromiumoxide-runner"` then `rm -f /private/var/folders/*/*/T/chromiumoxide-runner/Singleton*`. That glob legitimately matches NOTHING on some machines, and "no matches found" is not evidence the daemon is healthy. (b) *Capture wedged while the daemon still answers* — `navigate` and `eval` succeed, every `screenshot` times out with `request failed while the daemon PID was still alive`, and NO Chrome process survives (`ps aux | grep -c "[C]hrome for Testing"` → 0). Reproduces on a fresh daemon and a trivial page, so it is not a heavy page. The lock that matters is in the browser PROFILE: `pkill -9 -f "Chrome for Testing"; rm -f ~/.gsd-browser/browser-profile/Singleton* ~/.gsd-browser/daemon.pid ~/.gsd-browser/daemon.sock; gsd-browser daemon start`. Do NOT `gsd-browser daemon stop` first — it prints "Daemon stopped." and stops nothing, so it reads as a completed step that changed no state.
- **Clicking a force-directed canvas: dispatch on the ELEMENT, never `click --x --y`.** The simulation keeps moving nodes, so coordinates read by `eval` are stale by the time the click lands and it silently selects whichever node drifted under the point (this picked `SpecstoryIntegration` instead of `LiveLoggingSystem` twice in a row, reporting success both times). Find the `g.node` by label, then `for (const ev of ['pointerdown','mousedown','pointerup','mouseup','click']) el.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent(ev,{bubbles:true,cancelable:true,view:window}))`, and always assert afterwards on WHICH node ended up selected.
- **A viewer page can take minutes to first paint under gsd-browser** — `/viewer/coding` parses ~18MB of entities plus 18k relations and sits on "Loading coding graph…" with `Showing 0 of 0 nodes` the whole time. That is not the `localhost`-vs-`127.0.0.1` hang; check `gsd-browser network` for whether `/api/v1/entities` was even issued before concluding anything. Poll with a `Monitor` until-loop rather than a single long `eval`.
- **Constraint dodging is forbidden**: fix the underlying issue, don't swap APIs to pattern-match around a regex (e.g. `process.stderr.write` to dodge `no-console-log`). For legitimate exceptions, include `OVERRIDE_CONSTRAINT: <id>` with rationale.
- **km-core LLM proxy endpoint**: rapid-llm-proxy serves `POST /api/complete` (NOT OpenAI `/v1/chat/completions`) on port **12435** (host) / `host.docker.internal:12435` (container, pre-set as `LLM_CLI_PROXY_URL`). Don't confuse with port **3033** (Health API — silently 404s `Cannot POST /api/complete`). Body: `{ process, messages, complexity? }`; response: `{ content, provider, model, tokens, latencyMs }` (not OpenAI-wrapped; `provider` is the ACCOUNT id). URL precedence: `RAPID_LLM_PROXY_URL` → `LLM_CLI_PROXY_URL` → `LLM_PROXY_URL` → `http://localhost:${LLM_CLI_PROXY_PORT ?? '12435'}`, append `/api/complete` once. Canonical clients: `scripts/backfill-raw-observations.mjs:40,95` (host), `integrations/semantic-analysis/src/agents/llm-with-process.ts` (container). **`taskType` does nothing** — only the `complexity` band (via `bg-<process>` route in `llm-routing.yaml`, or per-request on a `from-caller` route) controls cost.
- **km-core reads MUST NOT write — pass `readOnly` on request-scoped opens**: `close()` persists by default; `persistGraph` writes the WHOLE graph under one LevelDB key, so a read-only open still rewrites it on close. Fine for a one-shot CLI, fatal for a polled HTTP route (caused a 550× disk-amplification OOM-kill loop on vkb-server via `/api/experiments/runs`). Use `openExperimentStore({ readOnly: true })` for any read-path handler. Diagnostic: one GET adding one ~1MB `.ldb` file, or an order-of-magnitude gap between `du -sh` of the LevelDB and its JSON export. Recovery: stop vkb-server, `launchctl bootout` the writers, move the leveldb dir aside, open+close once to let `hydrate()` rebuild from `.data/experiments/exports/*.json`.

## Feature Modularity

- **`coding` is composable — nine features, one resolver, `coding-features` to change them.** `lsl`, `observations`, `knowledge`, `codegraph`, `constraints`, `llm-proxy`, `performance`, `health`, `statusline`. Defaults are ALL-ON (= `full`, the developer profile incl. `lsl-redirect`); `install.sh` offers four tiers instead — `harness` (default, no Docker) → `learning` → `learning-perf` → `everything` — and always writes the choice. Retired names (`km`, `km-perf`, `proxy-only`, `logging-only`) are `alias:` entries in `config/feature-profiles.yaml`, hidden from listings. Config layers (last wins): built-in defaults → `config/features.yaml` (committed team default) → `~/.coding/features.yaml` (per-machine, what the dashboard writes) → `CODING_FEATURE_<ID>=on|off`. Edit via `coding-features set <id> on|off` / `profile <name>`, or the dashboard's **Features** tab. Full feature→artifact matrix: `docs/architecture/features.md`.
- **A dependent whose dependency is off is auto-disabled; the dependency is NEVER auto-enabled** (`observations`→`lsl`, `knowledge`→`observations`, `performance`→`llm-proxy`). The resolver records a reason string that every surface quotes verbatim — CLI, status line tooltip, dashboard chip — so "why is X off" has one answer everywhere.
- **Only `knowledge`, `codegraph` and `constraints` need Docker.** With all three off, `_start_services()` skips the container entirely and the launcher never demands a daemon — that is what makes the `harness` tier (and `minimal`) work on a machine without Docker Desktop. `health` deliberately does NOT need Docker (the coordinator and both dashboard servers have host implementations).
- **Fail-open vs fail-closed is deliberate and asymmetric.** Anything that STARTS a process (launcher, service starter, CLI guards) fails closed — an unparseable config aborts rather than half-starting. Anything that DISPLAYS (status line, dashboard, coordinator checks) fails open — showing everything plus an error, because a UI that silently loses half its content looks identical to a broken build.
- **Apply tiers**: `live` (status line, dashboard, coordinator checks, CLI gates — next read), `apply` (host daemons + container programs — `scripts/apply-features.mjs` diffs and starts/stops only the delta), `session` (agent hooks — `--settings` is fixed at launch, so new sessions only). The dashboard labels each rather than pretending everything is instant.
- **The `/features` API lives on the health COORDINATOR (:3034), not the dashboard server** — the dashboard runs inside the container and the file it edits (`~/.coding/features.yaml`) is on the host, plus applying runs `launchctl`/`systemctl`/`schtasks`. `server.js` reverse-proxies `/api/features`. One writer implementation: `lib/features/write.mjs`.
- **Adding a service/daemon/container program/tab/badge means declaring its feature.** Four mappings must agree (`lib/features/daemons.mjs`, `scripts/apply-features.mjs`, `docker/entrypoint.sh`, `docs/architecture/features.md`); `tests/features/*.test.mjs` fails the build when they drift. `bin/llm` is deliberately ungated — it queries Docker Model Runner, not rapid-llm-proxy.

- **A team is a SET OF REPOS** (`lib/teams/config.cjs`): `config/teams/<id>.json` (ontology) → `config/teams.yaml` (shipped, no memberships) → `~/.coding/teams.yaml` (user: membership, `active:`) → `CODING_TEAMS`. A team with no `repos`/`include` = the repo named like its id (the old basename meaning). `metadata.project` names the REPO (`projectIdFor`); membership is derived via `teamsOf`, never stamped. ONE scanner, `lib/teams/discover.mjs` (roots default `$HOME`, cache `<data home>/var/projects.json`, container maps `$HOME/Agentic`→`/workspace`). API on the coordinator `/teams`, dashboard proxy `/api/teams-config` (NOT `/api/teams` — obs-api's), **Teams** tab. Ref: `docs/architecture/teams.md`.
- **Learned knowledge is persisted PER PROJECT and shared by git** (T4, `docs/architecture/knowledge-sharing.md`): km-core hydrate is a UNION MERGE of LevelDB + every project's export (newest `updatedAt` wins, relations by `(from,type,to)`, deletions as `attributes.kmTombstones`) — never "pick the bigger copy". obs-api is the ONLY writer into `<repo>/.coding/kb/` (`lib/kb/layout.mjs` 'owner'); container stores read everything, write `exports/general.json` ('local'). Pull at launch, local commit at session end + every 30 min, push ONLY via `coding sync --push`. After a manual pull: `curl -X POST localhost:12436/api/kb/reload`. A pre-T4 deletion has no tombstone, so a stale LevelDB can resurrect it on the first merge — diff LevelDB vs the JSON export before trusting a restart after a SIGKILL.

## Available Skills

The following skills are available. When a task matches a skill's description,
read the full skill file and follow its instructions.

- **constraints** (`.claude/commands/constraints.md`): Check code or an action against this project's constraint rules, read compliance status and violation history, and add or amend rules. Use before writing code that might trip a guardrail, when a PreToolUse hook has blocked something and you need to see why, or when the user asks about constraints, guardrails or compliance. Replaces the former constraint-monitor MCP tools.
- **documentation-style** (`.claude/commands/documentation-style.md`): Enforce consistent styling for documentation artifacts (PlantUML, Mermaid, markdown, PNG diagrams). Invoke BEFORE creating or modifying any .puml file, generating PNGs from PlantUML, working with Mermaid diagrams, or updating documentation artifacts — and whenever the user mentions diagrams, PlantUML, PUML, PNG, visualization, or architecture diagrams.
- **experiment** (`.claude/commands/experiment.md`): Describe a cross-agent experiment in plain English (or with flags), then auto-run the matrix, compare, and render the ranked variant table
- **graphify** (`.claude/commands/graphify.md`): Query and rebuild the project's code knowledge graph (graphify). Use for any question about the codebase — architecture, "what calls X", "where is Y", file/function relationships, data-flow tracing — instead of blind greps. The graph is a static graph.json served over MCP by the coding-graphify container; rebuild it with `graphify update` when it's stale.
- **kgbench** (`.claude/commands/kgbench.md`): Run, resume, regrade and report the kgbench code-retrieval benchmark (coding-v1) across retrieval arms, agents and models — and diagnose the routing that decides which model actually answers. Also covers the Performance → Benchmarks dashboard sub-tab, the second front-end over the same scripts.
- **playwright-cli** (`.claude/commands/playwright-cli.md`): Use this skill whenever the user wants to automate a browser, scrape web content, take screenshots or PDFs of pages, fill out forms, click through UI flows, or run end-to-end tests — without using an MCP server. This skill drives Playwright directly from the bash_tool via Node.js scripts. Trigger whenever the user says things like "open this URL", "screenshot this page", "scrape this site", "automate this form", "test this UI", "extract data from", "click through", "check if this page works", or any task that requires real browser interaction. Prefer this skill over web_fetch when JavaScript rendering, authentication, interaction, or visual output is needed.
- **semantic** (`.claude/commands/semantic.md`): Run UKB knowledge-base workflows (wave-analysis and friends), manage the ontology, refresh stale knowledge entities, and reach the semantic-analysis tools. Use whenever the user says "ukb", "ukb full", "ukb debug", asks to run or check a knowledge workflow, or asks about ontology classes and entity refresh. Replaces the former semantic-analysis MCP tools.
- **sl** (`.claude/commands/sl.md`): Load session logs (LSL) from current and coding projects for continuity
